intro.text: The eldest of the three leaders who make up Beacon's ruling council on Canticle, and likely the oldest person in Beacon.

items.text: Compassion was born on Canticle and, late in life, named to the Greater Good of the Beaconite community, then under the Cinder King's rule. As an elder she was meant to be among the next turned into sunhearts to keep the community going, until Elegy, named Lodestar, ended the practice of sacrificing the eldest to seek the Refuge instead.

Hearing that Zeal's raid had recovered Elegy and the Cinder King's Scadrian key at great cost, including the life of Divinity, she said they had a duty to test the key and commended Zeal's team. When another council member warned that the Cinder King would chase them, she replied that he would seek to destroy them anyway; the theft had only hardened his resolve, as he relied on appearing unchallenged.

Learning that Nomad had survived seconds in the sunlight, she told him of the Sunlit Ones, who took in sunlight and built a city beneath the ground, and believed he was one of them, all the more when he read the key's Scadrian text. Trusting that Adonalsium would bless the search for the Refuge, she asked that the people of Beacon consent to it first.
In return for his help, the council agreed to give Nomad food, drink and clothing and to remove the bracers he had been put in by the Cinder King's forces.

When Jeffrey Jeffrey warned that the plan was dangerous, she agreed to make that clear to the people but said they had to hope in it as their sunhearts were dying, asking him to imagine proving that Canticle didn't need the Cinder King's false unity to survive.
As the council debated punishing Rebeke's insubordination, she stayed silent, speaking only to suggest that Rebeke see to Nomad's needs as her punishment.

Forced south into an untenable corridor, Compassion admitted to the Beaconites that they were trapped by the mountains with dwindling power. When Confidence questioned the purpose of crossing, she reminded her that a tiny hope was better than the alternative and that they owed it to their ancestors to try.

She watched Nomad's first prototype engine explode. When he said they must abandon all but Beacon's ten largest ships, she mourned Elegy's grand city of freedom, left for the sun, and noted they would be doomed if they did not find the Refuge.
After Beacon crashed beyond the mountains, she met with the city's leaders and Nomad in the hall of the Chorus, sitting on the ground wrapped in a blanket.
As Beacon fled along the mountain's shadow, she insisted every ship fly at its best speed and not slow for those in trouble.

After Nomad saved the straggling ship, the Greater Good drew him into a prayer circle, and Compassion told him the name Nomad no longer fit, as he had a place with them. Contemplation named him Zellion, which Compassion said meant One Who Finds. Now Connected, the Beaconites shared their warmth with him, and she said he had given them every moment they had.
When the Scadrian scientists allowed three people to join Zellion in negotiating, she asked Rebeke to go in her place so that the whole Greater Good wouldn't be at risk at once.

After the Cinder King's defeat, Compassion was the first to recognize what Rebeke had become. The Greater Good offered Rebeke the authority to lead, but she refused, saying they should remain in charge.

appearance.text: An elderly woman with dark ebony skin, light brown eyes and tight white curls, who wears the Greater Good's black dress, gloves and hat even indoors. Shorter, older and frailer than the others, she needs help to walk, and her small voice wavers, though she shows an inner strength.
Because of her age she is nearly always seated, on the floor if need be.

personality.text: She and her fellow council members treat one another with great respect, prefacing even disagreements with a phrase of deference.

Her empathy extends to Beacon's dead, whose memory and contributions she weighs in her decisions. She also understands her foes' motives, predicting the Cinder King's thinking from his drive to keep his authority.
She focuses on the physical and emotional welfare of her people and on the long term, which at times means valuing the survival of the many above that of one.
